text: An Australian wombat leaves droppings that look as if they came out of a mold: they are shaped like ___.
explanation: Georgia Tech researchers studied how corners form inside a wombat's intestine; the droppings are not shaped after they come out.

text: When decorating his display court, a male satin bowerbird collects clips, caps, and ornaments that are mostly ___.
explanation: The male decorates his court with blue objects, including human-made items such as clips and bottle caps.

text: A beaver's front teeth are naturally orange because their outer enamel contains ___.
explanation: Iron in the enamel gives the teeth their orange color; it does not come from leftover wood.

text: In a Queen Mary University experiment, bumblebees repeatedly returned to an activity with no food reward: rolling ___.
explanation: The bees voluntarily rolled wooden balls, displaying behavior that met the study's criteria for play.

text: One woodpecker species turns a whole tree trunk into a pantry by stuffing its holes with ___.
explanation: Acorn woodpeckers store nuts in drilled holes, turning the tree into a shared food store.

text: On moonless nights, a dung beetle species can keep a straight course using the light of the ___.
explanation: Experiments showed that Scarabaeus satyrus uses the galaxy's bright band as a reference while rolling its ball.
sourceHint: How do dung beetles' diets keep the world clean?
sourceTitle: How do dung beetles' diets keep the world clean?

text: The dark patches around a meerkat's eyes reduce glare, doing a job similar to ___.
explanation: Dark fur around the eyes reduces glare, helping an animal watch its surroundings in bright sunlight.

text: A reindeer's eyes adapt to the seasons: the reflective layer changes from gold in summer to ___ in winter.
explanation: The change happens in the reflective layer behind the retina, not the visible iris, and helps in dim winter light.
sourceHint: Opinion: How reindeer eyes transform in winter to give them twilight vision
sourceTitle: Opinion: How reindeer eyes transform in winter to give them twilight vision

text: A platypus closes its eyes underwater, but its bill detects ___ signals produced by its prey.
explanation: The bill contains electrical and mechanical receptors that help locate food underwater.

text: Both flamingo parents feed their chick a red, nutrient-rich secretion called ___.
explanation: Both parents produce crop milk. Despite its name, this secretion is not mammalian milk.
sourceHint: Practical Tips for Anyone Currently Raising Nine Flamingo Chicks at the Same Time
sourceTitle: Practical Tips for Anyone Currently Raising Nine Flamingo Chicks at the Same Time

text: The titan arum attracts certain insects with an unromantic scent resembling ___.
explanation: The titan arum's flower structure emits a carrion-like smell that attracts insects normally drawn to decomposing flesh.

text: Some mimosa plants react quickly when touched: they ___.
explanation: Sensitive mimosa leaves fold in response to touch; the plant itself does not move away.
sourceHint: Mimosa L. — Plants of the World Online
sourceTitle: Mimosa L. — Plants of the World Online

text: A desert welwitschia may look like a pile of green ribbons, but it has only ___ permanent true leaves.
explanation: Its two leaves keep growing and split into ribbons, making the plant appear to have many more.

text: A ripe squirting cucumber launches its seeds like a water pistol, firing them out with ___.
explanation: When the fruit separates from its stalk, pressurized liquid inside shoots out along with the seeds.

text: Some orchids use a romantic trick to attract pollinators: their flowers resemble ___.
explanation: Bee orchids mimic the appearance of females, attracting males that help transfer pollen.
sourceHint: Sneaky orchids and their pollination tricks
sourceTitle: Sneaky orchids and their pollination tricks

text: Unlike many familiar trees, cacao produces small flowers directly on its ___.
explanation: Many cacao flowers grow on the trunk and older branches, later developing into large seed-bearing pods.

text: Some pitcher plants offer nectar to tree shrews and receive a nutritious meal of ___ in return.
explanation: Plants such as Nepenthes rajah attract tree shrews to nectar above the pitcher, where their droppings provide nutrients.

text: An aquatic bladderwort trap rapidly draws in water and prey, rather like a ___.
explanation: When triggered, the tiny trap opens and sucks in water and prey; the comparison describes its capture mechanism.

text: Before a giant rafflesia flower appears, most of the hidden plant lives inside ___.
explanation: Rafflesia is a parasite living within a host vine's tissues and lacks ordinary leaves, roots, and stems.

text: The chocolate vine does not produce candy bars; its name comes from ___.
explanation: Akebia quinata flowers have a scent described as chocolate-like, among other notes; the name refers to their fragrance.

text: After grinding coral material, parrotfish produce droppings that can help form beaches as ___.
explanation: Some parrotfish grind limestone material swallowed while feeding, then excrete sand that contributes to certain beaches.

text: Antarctic icefish have almost transparent blood because they lack the pigment ___.
explanation: These fish lack hemoglobin, which gives most vertebrates' blood its red color.

text: Sea otters carry food in natural skin pockets located beneath their ___.
explanation: Loose skin folds beneath the front limbs provide pockets for storing gathered food.

text: After a salty seafood meal, marine iguanas visibly get rid of excess salt by ___.
explanation: Specialized glands remove salt, which is then sneezed out through the nose and can leave white deposits.
sourceHint: 5 facts that make the marine iguana a master of adaptation
sourceTitle: 5 facts that make the marine iguana a master of adaptation

text: Researchers offered tiny decorative balls to decorator crabs, which treated them as accessories and stuck them onto their ___.
explanation: Decorator crabs attach materials to their bodies as camouflage and accepted small artificial balls in the experiment.

text: To knock an insect into the water, an archerfish takes aim and fires ___ from its mouth.
explanation: Archerfish hit insects with a focused jet of water, then catch what falls in.
sourceHint: How This Fish Sharp Shoots Its Prey with Spit
sourceTitle: How This Fish Sharp Shoots Its Prey with Spit

text: A mantis shrimp's punch is so fast that it creates bubbles of ___ in the water.
explanation: The strike causes cavitation and rapidly collapsing vapor bubbles; they are not the animal's breath.

text: In the deep sea, a yeti crab species farms food on its hairy arms: its crop is ___.
explanation: Bacteria live on the bristles of some yeti crabs, providing food near deep-sea seep environments.

text: Some pearlfish choose a strange living home, hiding inside a ___.
explanation: Some pearlfish shelter inside sea cucumbers; their name does not mean they live inside pearls.

text: While eating, certain sea stars can push part of their ___ out through their mouths.
explanation: The cardiac stomach extends outside the body and begins digesting prey before the process continues internally.
sourceHint: Echinoderms: Sea Stars, Urchins, Sand Dollars, and Relatives
sourceTitle: Echinoderms: Sea Stars, Urchins, Sand Dollars, and Relatives

text: The Juno probe carried a small Galileo figure holding a telescope, made in the style of ___ toys.
explanation: Juno carried figures of Galileo, Jupiter, and Juno in LEGO style; the flight versions were made of aluminum.

text: Moon trees grow on Earth; the part that orbited the Moon during Apollo 14 was their ___.
explanation: Stuart Roosa carried tree seeds in lunar orbit, and they were planted after returning to Earth.

text: During Gemini 6, mission control was surprised to hear Jingle Bells played in space on a ___.
explanation: Wally Schirra brought a small harmonica, while Thomas Stafford accompanied him with bells.

text: Some Apollo astronauts said lunar dust brought into their cabin smelled like ___.
explanation: They described the smell after the dust entered the spacecraft's air, not by smelling it in the Moon's vacuum.
sourceHint: Digging In: When Rovers Get Dirt on Mars - S4E11
sourceTitle: Digging In: When Rovers Get Dirt on Mars - S4E11

text: Tortillas work well on space menus partly because they do not fill the cabin with ___.
explanation: Tortillas do not crumble like ordinary bread, whose loose crumbs can float around the spacecraft.

text: Cassini found small lakes in northern Titan, but their main liquid is not water; it is ___.
explanation: Cassini measurements showed these northern lakes are rich in liquid methane in a world far colder than Earth.
sourceHint: Cassini Reveals Surprises with Titan’s Lakes
sourceTitle: Cassini Reveals Surprises with Titan’s Lakes

text: During a demonstration on the Moon, David Scott dropped a hammer and a ___ together, and both landed at the same time.
explanation: The Apollo 15 astronaut demonstrated free fall without air resistance using a hammer and a falcon feather.

text: Each Voyager probe carried sounds and pictures greeting possible extraterrestrial life, stored on a ___.
explanation: The message is a gold-plated copper record containing sounds, pictures, and instructions for playback.

text: Alan Shepard turned a sample-collecting tool into sporting equipment and played ___ on the Moon.
explanation: He attached a golf-club head to a sampling tool and hit balls near the end of his Apollo 14 moonwalk.
sourceHint: Apollo 14 Demonstrated Spaceflight Challenges Are Solvable
sourceTitle: Apollo 14 Demonstrated Spaceflight Challenges Are Solvable

text: A special Italian machine reached the International Space Station to prepare a familiar earthly treat: ___.
explanation: Samantha Cristoforetti used the ISSpresso machine to prepare espresso aboard the station in 2015.
sourceHint: Food on the International Space Station
sourceTitle: Food on the International Space Station

text: Before Play-Doh became a children's toy, it was sold as a material for cleaning ___.
explanation: The product began as a paste for removing dirt from wallpaper before being repackaged as modeling material for children.

text: While working on ship equipment, Richard James watched a fallen spring bounce and was inspired to create ___.
explanation: James was developing springs for naval equipment when one inspired the toy that walks down stairs.

text: Lonnie Johnson was experimenting with a heat-pump system when a burst of water inspired a ___.
explanation: A heat-pump experiment led to the idea Johnson later developed into the Super Soaker.
sourceHint: Meet Lonnie Johnson, the Man Behind the Super Soaker
sourceTitle: Meet Lonnie Johnson, the Man Behind the Super Soaker

text: Annoyed that her dishes broke during cleaning, Josephine Cochrane developed a practical machine for ___.
explanation: Cochrane designed a dishwasher using water and racks to hold the dishes, then turned it into a commercial product.

text: When Melitta Bentz experimented with a coffee filter, she took blotting paper from ___.
explanation: Bentz put blotting paper from her son's notebook into a perforated container, beginning the paper coffee filter.

text: After seeing a driver repeatedly remove snow from his window, Mary Anderson invented the ___.
explanation: A winter streetcar ride inspired a mechanism that let a driver wipe the glass using a lever from inside.
sourceHint: Mary Anderson: The Unheralded Inventor of the Windshield Wiper
sourceTitle: Mary Anderson: The Unheralded Inventor of the Windshield Wiper

text: In Edison's first phonograph, a needle recorded sound on a cylinder covered in ___.
explanation: The first model recorded vibrations by pressing a needle into tin foil wrapped around a cylinder.

text: To make the ridges in his bendable-straw prototype, Joseph Friedman put a screw inside a straw and pressed around it with ___.
explanation: He wrapped floss around the screw's grooves through the paper straw, creating a corrugated section that could bend.
sourceHint: The Straight Truth About the Flexible Drinking Straw
sourceTitle: The Straight Truth About the Flexible Drinking Straw

text: Margaret Knight developed a machine that lets a paper bag stand like a little box by giving it a ___.
explanation: Knight's machine cut, folded, and glued paper into flat-bottomed bags instead of envelope-shaped ones.

text: Chester Greenwood's invention used two pads joined by a band to protect the ___ from cold.
explanation: Greenwood developed and patented earmuffs, using connected pads to keep the ears warm.

text: Long before Mario and game consoles, Nintendo began by making ___.
explanation: Nintendo first made illustrated Japanese hanafuda cards, years before moving into electronic games.

text: The game that preceded Monopoly was designed to warn players about an economic problem: ___.
explanation: Elizabeth Magie created The Landlord's Game to illustrate the effects of concentrated wealth and property ownership.

text: An Etch A Sketch stylus does not use ink; it draws by removing a layer of ___ from the glass.
explanation: The knobs move an internal stylus that clears powder from the glass, while shaking redistributes it to erase the lines.

text: John Lloyd Wright's Lincoln Logs were inspired by Japanese building designs intended to withstand ___.
explanation: Interlocking timber construction inspired small wooden pieces that could be joined to build toy houses.

text: The first version of Hasbro's toy with interchangeable faces and limbs sold only the parts; families had to provide ___.
explanation: The original Mr. Potato Head pieces were attached to real potatoes or other vegetables before plastic bodies were introduced.

text: The name Pac-Man comes from the Japanese expression paku-paku, which imitates the action of ___.
explanation: The name reflects opening and closing the mouth while eating, fitting a character that gobbles dots.

text: Stretch Armstrong can be pulled and return to shape partly because it is filled with ___.
explanation: The rubber toy contains thick corn syrup that helps it stretch and recover its shape.
sourceHint: Magic Slate, Stretch Armstrong, and Toys that Make You Go Hmmm…
sourceTitle: Magic Slate, Stretch Armstrong, and Toys that Make You Go Hmmm…

text: Cluedo's creator encountered hotel murder-mystery entertainment while working as a ___.
explanation: Anthony Pratt played piano at venues hosting mystery evenings before inventing the detective board game.

text: The original Easy-Bake Oven baked cakes using heat from an unusual cooking source: ___.
explanation: The small oven used heat from incandescent light bulbs before later versions changed the technology.

text: Eleanor Abbott designed Candy Land to entertain children spending time in ___.
explanation: Abbott created the game while recovering from polio to entertain children in hospital wards.

text: Thousands of years ago, Nanni wrote a complaint to the merchant Ea-nasir on a clay tablet about the quality of ___.
explanation: The British Museum preserves the complaint about poor-quality copper and the treatment of the buyer's representative.
sourceHint: 29 things you (probably) didn't know about the British Museum
sourceTitle: 29 things you (probably) didn't know about the British Museum

text: Some warriors among the ancient Lewis chess pieces look especially fierce because they are biting their ___.
explanation: Some warder pieces depict shield-biting warriors, associated with berserkers in Norse tradition.
sourceHint: Redisplay of the Lewis chess pieces allows them to be seen in full for the first time
sourceTitle: Redisplay of the Lewis chess pieces allows them to be seen in full for the first time

text: Readers in Hereford Cathedral's historic library could open books, but removing them was difficult because they were attached to ___.
explanation: The chained-library system allowed reading while protecting valuable volumes against theft.

text: Ancient Egyptians buried shabti figures with the dead, believing the figures could perform ___ on their behalf.
explanation: Shabti inscriptions describe the figure substituting for its owner in agricultural labor in the afterlife, according to ancient Egyptian belief.

text: A Roman letter found at Vindolanda mentions a shipment of socks, shoes, and another practical item: ___.
explanation: The writing tablet records clothing sent to its recipient, including socks, sandals, and underwear.

text: The shimmer of Ellen Terry's Lady Macbeth costume came from more than sequins; it was decorated with ___.
explanation: Shiny beetle wing cases give the dress a green surface whose appearance changes with the light.

text: The Roman Lycurgus Cup looks green in reflected light, but turns red when ___.
explanation: Tiny metal particles in the glass make it appear different colors in reflected and transmitted light.
sourceHint: Large print guide — Room 41: Sutton Hoo and Europe
sourceTitle: Large print guide — Room 41: Sutton Hoo and Europe

text: A samurai helmet in the Metropolitan Museum resembles an unexpectedly gentle creature: a crouching ___.
explanation: The Japanese helmet is shaped like a crouching rabbit, complete with long ears above the head.
sourceHint: Helmet in the Shape of a Crouching Rabbit
sourceTitle: Helmet in the Shape of a Crouching Rabbit

text: A crocodile mummy from Kom Ombo in the British Museum carries an unexpected group on its back: ___.
explanation: Mummified young crocodiles were attached to reed supports on the larger animal's back and covered with resin.

text: Mysterious Roman metal objects with holes in their faces have been discovered; each of these objects has ___ faces.
explanation: Known as Roman dodecahedra, their shape is clear but their original purpose remains debated.
sourceHint: The mysterious dodecahedra of the Roman Empire
sourceTitle: The mysterious dodecahedra of the Roman Empire

text: The spice mace is not a leaf; it is the red covering around the seed of ___.
explanation: The same fruit provides two spices: its seed and the surrounding covering, which is dried to make mace.
sourceHint: A spice sensation in oils at the Marianne North Gallery
sourceTitle: A spice sensation in oils at the Marianne North Gallery

text: The cinnamon stick floating in your cup is not a twig; it is a curled piece of ___.
explanation: Cinnamon sticks are made from inner bark that curls as it dries, not whole branches.
sourceHint: A spice sensation in oils at the Marianne North Gallery
sourceTitle: A spice sensation in oils at the Marianne North Gallery

text: The small capers pickled for appetizers are not seeds; they are ___.
explanation: The familiar condiment uses flower buds before they open; the plant's fruit can also be pickled separately.
sourceHint: Capparaceae Juss. — Plants of the World Online
sourceTitle: Capparaceae Juss. — Plants of the World Online

text: Cacao beans were more than an ingredient for a drink to the Aztecs; they were also used as ___.
explanation: The Aztecs used cacao beans for exchange, giving them value beyond making drinks.

text: The name allspice suggests a mixture, but it is actually ___.
explanation: Allspice comes from the dried unripe fruit of one plant, named for the range of aromas it recalls.
sourceHint: Christmas spice makes all things nice
sourceTitle: Christmas spice makes all things nice

text: Momofuku Ando found the key to drying instant noodles while watching his wife fry ___.
explanation: He noticed moisture leaving tempura batter in hot oil and experimented with flash-frying noodles.

text: In a 1957 television prank, the BBC showed farmers supposedly harvesting ___ from trees.
explanation: The report was an April Fools' hoax: spaghetti does not grow on trees, however convincing the harvest looked.

text: John Young hid an unlisted meal in his suit for Gemini 3: a ___.
explanation: Young produced the sandwich during the flight, where its loose crumbs posed a practical problem in the cabin.
sourceHint: Contraband Corned Beef and the Early Days of Space Biology: the Gemini III Mission
sourceTitle: Contraband Corned Beef and the Early Days of Space Biology: the Gemini III Mission

text: A Victorian Mrs. Beeton soup recipe calls for a ketchup made not from tomatoes but from ___.
explanation: Her turkey soup recipe includes mushroom ketchup; historically, ketchup referred to sauces beyond tomato varieties.
sourceHint: Is Mrs Beeton Relevant to Modern Families?
sourceTitle: Is Mrs Beeton Relevant to Modern Families?

text: The sapodilla tree provides fruit and a substance called chicle, historically used to make ___.
explanation: Chicle is extracted from the tree's milky sap and was used as a natural base for chewing gum.
sourceHint: Manilkara zapota (L.) P.Royen — Plants of the World Online
sourceTitle: Manilkara zapota (L.) P.Royen — Plants of the World Online

text: Picasso joined a saddle and handlebars to make Bull's Head; both parts originally belonged to a ___.
explanation: The saddle forms the head and the handlebars the horns, changing their meaning without hiding their original purpose.

text: Andy Warhol saved letters, clippings, and everyday objects in time capsules whose usual container was a ___.
explanation: Warhol sealed everyday materials in boxes, creating an archive known as his Time Capsules.

text: Henri Matisse described making shapes from colored paper as drawing with ___.
explanation: He cut shapes from gouache-painted paper and arranged them, creating forms through cutting rather than outlining them with a pencil.

text: With de Kooning's permission, Robert Rauschenberg obtained one of his drawings and made a new artwork by ___.
explanation: De Kooning agreed to provide a drawing for Rauschenberg to erase, resulting in Erased de Kooning Drawing.
sourceHint: Robert Rauschenberg, Erased de Kooning Drawing, 1953
sourceTitle: Robert Rauschenberg, Erased de Kooning Drawing, 1953

text: John Cage's 4 minutes 33 seconds instructs performers to ___ throughout its three movements.
decoys: Strike the piano with their hands
explanation: Performers produce no intentional notes, drawing attention to surrounding sounds rather than requiring the whole world to be silent.
sourceHint: There Will Never Be Silence: Scoring John Cage’s 4′33″
sourceTitle: There Will Never Be Silence: Scoring John Cage’s 4′33″

text: Magritte painted a pipe and wrote a surprising statement beneath it: This is ___.
explanation: The Treachery of Images reminds viewers that a picture of a pipe is not an actual usable pipe.
sourceHint: The Treachery of Images (This is Not a Pipe)
sourceTitle: The Treachery of Images (This is Not a Pipe)

text: Composer Leroy Anderson brought an office machine into the orchestra for its taps and bell: a ___.
explanation: The Typewriter uses the actual machine as a percussion instrument, including its keys, bell, and carriage.

text: Meret Oppenheim turned a cup, saucer, and spoon into a surreal artwork by covering them in ___.
explanation: Fur covers the drinking utensils in Object, making familiar items appear strange and difficult to use.

text: Marcel Duchamp called his artwork Fountain, but the ready-made object he selected was a ___.
explanation: He presented a ready-made urinal as art, producing one of the best-known examples of the readymade.

text: On Dali's surreal telephone, a model seafood animal sits above the receiver: a ___.
explanation: Lobster Telephone combines a working telephone and a model lobster, joining two objects not normally associated.

text: In Vanuatu, special waterproof postcards can be mailed from a post office located ___.
explanation: Vanuatu offers special cards for its underwater post office near Hideaway Island, with mail collected by divers.

text: When the Eiffel Tower opened in 1889, it was not gray; its color was ___.
explanation: The tower has had several paint colors; its administration records reddish brown for its 1889 opening.
sourceHint: Painting and color of the Eiffel Tower
sourceTitle: Painting and color of the Eiffel Tower

text: A global vault inside a mountain in Svalbard protects ___.
explanation: The Svalbard vault stores backup seed collections to help safeguard agricultural diversity.

text: Gaudi wanted visitors to the Sagrada Familia to feel inside a forest, so he designed its columns to ___.
explanation: The stone columns branch to support the building and evoke the feeling of a forest inside the church.
sourceHint: Sagrada Família columns: the geometry, mechanics and materials of a stone forest
sourceTitle: Sagrada Família columns: the geometry, mechanics and materials of a stone forest

text: Antarctica's Blood Falls is not blood: the brine flowing from it is rich in ___.
explanation: The red color is associated with iron-rich brine emerging from beneath the ice.
sourceHint: Science on the Ice: The United States Antarctic Program
sourceTitle: Science on the Ice: The United States Antarctic Program

text: The star-like lights in some New Zealand caves come from glowworms, which are actually ___.
explanation: These local glowworms are the larval stage of small flies, using light to lure prey into sticky threads.
sourceHint: Clifden area: Places to go in Southland
sourceTitle: Clifden area: Places to go in Southland

text: The Giant's Causeway columns look precisely cut, but their regular shapes formed when ___ cracked as it cooled.
explanation: Basaltic lava cooled and contracted, forming cracks that created the polygonal columns seen today.

text: The brilliant white terraces of Pamukkale in Turkey are not snow; they are deposits of ___.
explanation: Mineral-rich spring water deposits material that builds the terraces; fresh calcium carbonate gives them their white appearance.

text: After rain, part of Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni salt flat resembles an enormous ___.
explanation: A reflective layer of water covers the flat surface during the wet season, making it mirror the sky.

text: The asymmetric shape of Venetian gondolas makes it easier to propel and steer them using ___.
explanation: The official Veneto source explains that the asymmetric hull counters the sideways force from its single oar, helping maintain direction.
sourceHint: Venezia, gondole — Bollettino Ufficiale Regione Veneto 5/2009, p. 1
sourceTitle: Venezia, gondole — Bollettino Ufficiale Regione Veneto 5/2009, p. 1
